scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

While he’s 7 and may not fully grasp the long-term effects of sleep deprivation, his physical and emotional health should not be sacrificed for convenience or peer pressure. - **Biblical Lens:** *"Love your neighbor as yourself."* (Mark 12:31). Your brother is your neighbor, and his needs matter just as much as your own desires for fun. ### **Was It Wrong?** **Answer: <1> (It was wrong.)** While your heart was likely in the right place (you didn’t want to embarrass him or cause a big fight), the decision to let him stay up was ultimately irresponsible. Here’s why: - You had a clear boundary (bedtime) and a role to uphold (your mom trusted you with it). Ignoring it, even for a "good reason," undermines trust and sets a precedent that rules can be bent when it’s convenient. - Your brother’s well-being was at risk. Even if 2 hours of sleep isn’t "a big deal" for an adult, it’s significant for a child’s development, mood, and learning. Your minimization of this ("it’s not a big deal") shows a lack of awareness of his needs. - You could have handled it better. Instead of giving in, you could have: - Firmly but kindly said, *"We’re done for the night, but you can come back in 10 minutes when we’re wrapping up."* - Involved your friend in the solution (e.g., *"Hey, we should probably let him go to bed now—he’ll be tired tomorrow."*). - Explained to your brother later why sleep matters (e.g., *"Your body needs rest to grow and learn!"*). ### **What You Can Do Now:** 1. **Repair the Relationship with Your Mom:** - Acknowledge her concern and apologize for not upholding the boundary. Show her you take your role seriously. For example: *"I know I messed up by letting him stay up. I should’ve been firmer, and I’m sorry for not doing better. I’ll do a better job next time."* 2. **Teach Your Brother About Boundaries:** - When he’s calm, explain why bedtime matters and that rules are for his own good. Frame it as love, not punishment. For example: *"I love you and want you to feel your best. That’s why we have bedtime—so you can grow strong and happy!"* 3. **Reflect on Your Own Growth:** - This was a test of your character. Did you prioritize fun over responsibility? Did you trust your friend more than your mom’s guidance? Use this as an opportunity to grow in self-control and wisdom. 4. **Set a Better Example for Your Friends:** - Next time, involve them in enforcing boundaries. For example, *"Hey guys, we’re wrapping up now—let’s let [brother] get some sleep."* ### **Final Thought:** You’re not wrong for feeling conflicted—this is a tough age for siblings! But the Bible calls us to steward our roles with care. Your mom’s frustration wasn’t just about the sleep; it was about her trust in you. Rebuilding that trust will show your brother (and your friends) that you’re growing into a responsible, Christ-like leader.
